epistemicQualifiers.claimText: we're going to do this — requesting access, at least up to the Presidency of the Republic, because the order has to come from the top down
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: Therefore, there was no sense, in this first hearing, Deputy, in bringing military personnel here to hear this. First, we need to set out what is happening, explicitly and publicly state it so they can provide information within the scope of the law, because we have been requesting this for a long time, since the law came into effect. We access Gov.br, which is the platform where each person has their own record. Today, everyone files their income tax through Gov.br, everyone has this right, and the LAI (Law on Access to Information) facilitates this. We access Cidic — the Document Indexing Code that contains Classified Information — and search for this information, but we cannot find it, there is no way to find it using the LAI, understand, Deputy? This is our problem. We need to address this issue using, of course, the Commission, the power the Commission has to enforce this, because these documents need to be made public. The LAI itself mandates that these documents be placed in a hall of declassified or classified documents. It's like looking for a needle in a haystack, because it's an enormous code. We have some examples here of our attempts. It's an enormous code, and there's no way to say: "Look, if this is classified, what information does it contain on UFO matters?" There's no way to identify this to request the document through the LAI. It's very specific. The LAI can be good today, for example, when you already know the subject. Then, if you activate the LAI: "Look, the subject is this, I'm interested in this and that, and this is the information I want." The LAI provides that information. But old documents, especially those from before the Constitution, we have no access to. For example, we have the films from Operation Prato. Indeed, Thiago has already accessed frames from this film, it's at least 15 minutes of footage. Where is it? We've already requested it from the Air Force, the process reached the Controladoria-Geral da União, but it stopped there. The official, who said they don't have this information, has public faith. So, it's there in the LAI, but it stopped there and there's no further recourse. This is a difficulty that the CBU faces. Unfortunately, we once again have to appeal to our beloved Deputy Chico Alencar, our ufological deputy. Thank God we have a deputy open to this subject, who makes it public, makes the Chamber fulfill its role, which is to bring this serious matter to debate. Here, we didn't go into details due to time constraints, but this is very serious and has a religious and political impact. There was interference from the United States in the case, violating our sovereignty, because they took the debris of the fallen object to Varginha. This had to have generated documentation. We tried, Deputy, even with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, to obtain documents attesting to the departure of these objects, of the creatures. There are none, there's no way to access this via LAI. Therefore, our denunciation is on record. We are making this denunciation and once again — I don't know how we're going to do this — requesting access, at least up to the Presidency of the Republic, because the order has to come from the top down. We requested assistance from the Office of the President, from the Civil House, as we did with the UFO Brazil Dossier, and we gained access. As the Deputy said, there are over 10,000 documents at the National Archives. As the late Gevaerd would say, it's all just window dressing. There's much more serious stuff hidden by the military power. I don't know by whose order, but the people have a right to access this.

epistemicQualifiers.claimText: you were present at the opening — to central issues of everyday life, such as the massacre in Gaza, the war in Ukraine, Brazilian social inequalities, and the attempt at a new coup with an amnesty bill whose text no one has seen yet in Congress
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: I want to apologize to the guests because he turned to adjectivization, to disqualifying a conversation that some may not like, may find unreal. But there is a dedication on our part, as I mentioned at the beginning — I don't know if you were present at the opening — to central issues of everyday life, such as the massacre in Gaza, the war in Ukraine, Brazilian social inequalities, and the attempt at a new coup with an amnesty bill whose text no one has seen yet in Congress. That falls within our concerns. THE MR. VICTOR RATTES - I would like to request the right of reply, President. THE MR. PRESIDENT (Chico Alencar. Block/PSOL - RJ) - No, there are other registered here. You already had your time and finished speaking before 2 minutes. Now it's our turn, Carlos, please. (Pause.) I apologize for the offense he subtly made, even with his attire, to mock, but everything is alright. Everyone dress as they wish, of course. You can't come here naked, because that's an insult to modesty. Now, in abundance, there are attacks on ethics and decorum in Congress. (Pause.) I'll come back to the topic quickly, for 2 minutes, so Thiago can explain what ufology is. Some may not understand this. THE MR. THIAGO LUIZ TICCHETTI - Unfortunately, Victor mixed the wheat with the chaff. If he knew a little about ufology, he would see that we are against that ET Bilu. Victor, it's much more than a partisan and political debate, because everyone has their political stance, we are dealing with freedom of information and a citizen's right, something you should be fighting for, something you should be advocating. (Inaudible intervention outside the microphone.) No, we are here discussing a topic, and any topic can be raised in the Legislative Commission on Participatory Legislation. We went after it and managed to get a Deputy to support us. That's all it was. Don't say that everyone here is a clown, that this is a circus. There are no clowns here. These are people who investigate, devote their lives and family time to serious research. So, when you speak, speak in a different way, in a polite manner. Don't put everyone in the same potato sack, no. Is that okay?

epistemicQualifiers.claimText: it is extremely timely - to speak about two very important aspects: rights and duties
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: MR. CARLOS ODONE DA COSTA NUNES - Thank you very much. Good morning everyone. I am grateful for the initiative of Deputy Chico Alencar in providing ufologists with the opportunity to discuss a so serious and grave topic, as has been brought up here on several occasions. Therefore, it is an honor for me to participate in this public hearing as the Secretary of the Brazilian Commission of Ufologists - CBU. Ufology is a topic of extreme importance, and I would say, of a very special significance, as it concerns all of us, the terrestrial humanity. I take this opportunity - I believe it is extremely timely - to speak about two very important aspects: rights and duties. Backed by the LAI, we have the right to know about everything that is happening, about the truth of the occurrences that marked UFO phenomenon manifestations in our country. I am referring to the events in Varginha and the cases related to Operation Plate in the Northern region of Brazil, especially regarding what was and continues to be hidden. This cover-up demands an opening without restrictions. The CBU, established in 1996, has already reached almost 3 decades of relentless struggle in search of answers, in search of the truth about all the events that have occurred in this country. The Brazilian Commission of Ufologists has not spared efforts during this entire period of almost 30 years, performing an unwavering work until reaching this historic public hearing situation. Therefore, Mr. Deputy, it is time for the Brazilian society to unite to make the uncovering a wake-up call for consciousness, so that it represents that we are, with much awareness, taking knowledge that we are visited, accompanied, monitored. With all this, the old slogan that everyone here knows applies: They are among us.

epistemicQualifiers.claimText: you've seen a very well-made film called Conclave
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: I would like to express my sincere thanks to Jackson Camargo, Paulo Henrique Baraky Werner, Arthur Paredes, Maria Valdete Leite, Jerbialdo Silva, Leandro Antonio dos Santos, João Marcelo Marques, Gener Silva, Jean Carlos Quintas Vieira, Robert de Souza, Eduardo Rodrigues de Oliveira, Yasser Flavio Rabello, Daniel Coimbra, João Batista Trigo, João Marcelo Marques, Carlos Augusto Alba, Rogério Ribeiro da Silva, and Claudio Aparecido for their interactions. I very much appreciate all your very interesting questions, which would deserve a hearing, a 4-hour or 5-hour dialogue. Critiques or affirmations about ufology question this type of theme — interested, because they are asking — or praise it. I will pass the questions to the entities here represented, so that they will send us the answer later. Our mandate is available to serve as a channel for this dialogue. We are not here to defend thesis A, B, or C as absolute truth, because absolute truth and dogma belong to the religious sphere. I have mine, thank God. Now, in the field of science, debate, controversy, dialectic, doubt is what drives humanity. By the way, I don't know if you've seen a very well-made film called Conclave. There's a candidate for Pope — I rooted for him, indeed, in the movie, in the fiction — who comes to a disturbing conclusion that, in short, God is doubt itself, God is the great question of the universe. He was not elected. By the way, a surprising one entered. Well, I'm not going to give away the spoiler. Finally, I will give one minute each to every member of the Board, thanking everyone, including Victor, who dismissed this hearing. But he has every right, too. Because no. We are here. You know you have all the space. It is now Mr. [Name]'s turn to speak. Vitório Pacaccini Tavares Paes. THE MR. VITÓRIO PACACCINI TAVARES PAES - Gentlemen, I am very grateful to all of you, on my behalf. 20/16

epistemicQualifiers.claimText: it's important to point out that all the recent Presidents of the United States have included ufology in their platforms—that "If elected
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: Who, in our country, is better equipped to record these phenomena than the person who gave testimony and treated it as if it were entirely outside the realm of credibility? It's our military, and they are the ones who have been generating this type of documentation. I ask, Deputy: why didn't Lieutenant-Brigadier Moreira Lima seek out—note that this is not against science, as I defend it—some scientist to speak about what he told me? Why did Sócrates Monteiro never do that? Because, often, very serious people from the scientific field find themselves unable to take a position in favor of what we advocate, precisely because of this completely absurd type of thinking after so many years of evidence recorded worldwide. I am not a supporter of any type of American politics nor will I defend any of them, but I think it's important to point out that all the recent Presidents of the United States have included ufology in their platforms—that "If elected..." story. That one is not a serious country either, because it handles it from its Presidents. Could these Presidents also have no idea what is science and what is not? Science certainly is not what was presented or argued here. (Applause.) MR. FERNANDO DE ARAGÃO RAMALHO - Just to conclude, since our colleagues have already said everything, I would suggest to that person to go to the National Archives. Here is the translation of the text from Brazilian Portuguese to English: Here is the report that Lieutenant-Brigadier Júlio Moreira Lima was supposed to release. A CBU managed to obtain access to the document, which does not mention "extraterrestrial" but states that it is intelligent and not our technology or American technology. That put on a show for the FAB jets. It was traveling at Mach 15. What kind of technology is this? Where does it come from? The very brigadier who signs the report says: "This is not ours. It may not be crewed, but it's intelligent. Our friend, who is an astronomer, could at least suggest where it comes from. Obviously, we are open to discussion. But where does that come from? It is a topic of study in ufology. If this isn't science, what is it? Ask the military, go to the National Archives, study ufology. Don't just criticize, like the guy who came here and talked a lot of nonsense without knowledge. That is bias and exists within the Academy. Let it be perfectly clear: discussing ufology within academia is taboo. Thank God, some universities already have PhD programs in the field — people are talking about the topic. A person who brings up such a conversation is totally out of touch. That's pure prejudice. (Applause.) MR. PRESIDENT (Chico Alencar. Block/PSOL - RJ) - I thank everyone again, including those who participated indirectly, regardless of their opinions. I'm also from the Academy. I came to see Doctor a bit out of the ordinary — a citizen not senile, not old, but already old. I have a great appreciation for science, but I think the explanation of the world does not end there. I am not dogmatic.

epistemicQualifiers.claimText: that it is the role of the Government to create support mechanisms for agriculture, such as the Disaster Fund
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: MR. EDUARDO SCIARRA (DEM-PR. Without revision of the speaker.) – Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, I request that the statement I am about to deliver be considered as read, in which I express our disappointment that the 2011/2012 Crop Plan, announced by the Federal Government last week, does not contain any reference to the Disaster Fund. This House, the National Congress as a whole, has approved over several years all the necessary regulations for the implementation of this fund, which will mitigate the suffering of rural producers who work outdoors in a high-risk activity. We have built all the legislative framework for this, including breaking the monopoly of reinsurance in Brazil. However, unfortunately, it has not yet been regulated, and the decree that should resolve this situation, unfortunately, will not meet the needs of this crop. STATEMENT DELIVERED BY THE SPEAKER Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, last week the Government launched the 2011/2012 Crop Plan. In my view, the Federal Government missed the opportunity to regulate the Disaster Fund. The law that created the Fund was sanctioned by the President of the Republic last August with the promise to apply 4 billion reais through public securities. However, to this day, almost a year later, the Government has not made the regulation, which, in practice, renders ineffective all the effort of the Congress in the discussion of this important legal instrument. Worse: rural producers will once again face a crop, assuming all the risks inherent to their activity. I am well acquainted with the dilemmas of Brazilian rural producers. A rural property is a business open to the sky, subject to rains, droughts, and all kinds of weather conditions. The regulation of the law will bring more security to farmers in times of adverse climatic events. Therefore, this delay is unacceptable, considering that the Legislature has worked for several years to remove an endless series of difficulties, and rural producers are disappointed with this decision, as they expected to count on the protection of the Fund for this year's crop. It is worth noting that this sector accounts for a significant portion of the national GDP, but it is the only one to bear all the risks inherent to its activities. I believe that it is the role of the Government to create support mechanisms for agriculture, such as the Disaster Fund. The main objective of the Disaster Fund is to make agricultural insurance viable through the creation of a private consortium composed of insurance companies and reinsurers, which would benefit from Federal Government subsidies. The consortium would be responsible for management and coverage.

We have followed with great zeal this project that deals with food and nutritional security and the human right to food provided by strengthening family farming - in this case, the creation of the MERCOSUR Fund for Support of Family Farming. We had the opportunity, in the Constitution, Justice and Citizenship Commission, to cast a favorable vote for its arrival in this House's plenary session. It is important to show Brazil's role and the weight of its financial contribution to this Fund, which is 70%, while Argentina's is 27%, Paraguay's is 1%, and Uruguay's is 2%. Although, mind you, the resources are still scarce, this has a symbolism: the integration of South America in favor of the small rural producers of family farming. At the same time, it translates this vision of international solidarity partnership, based on the spirit of equity and social justice. Since we are the largest and richest nation of this MERCOSUR unit, of course we have to make a proportionally larger contribution. It is in this sense that we hope this House will sign on, vote favorably, so that, in fact, this Fund can continue this work that we have already built over the course of the Lula government and that continues in the Dilma government, expanding access to food, improving production from family farming - which, as we know and was confirmed by the 2006 Agro-Pecuarian Census, is the great producer of our food, of the food that reaches our tables, in contrast to large corporate farming, which works more for export. It is family farming, as we confirmed now, at the Latin America Hunger Combat Front meeting in Colombia, the great axis of hunger and malnutrition combat. Therefore, it is increasingly necessary that Latin American nations unite to eradicate hunger and poverty from this continent. That is all I had to say, Mr. President. Thank you very much. epistemicQualifiers.claimText: this is a good opportunity for Parliament to reflect on a fundamental issue for the country, and that instead of dividing us, it should unite us
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: Mr. President, ladies and gentlemen Members, interviews with the Governor of Sergipe, Marcelo Déda, were published yesterday in Valor Econômico and today in Estado, expressing his opinions on tax reform and the pre-salt. Déda stated that tax reform cannot merely mean the unification of ICMS with the Northeast, North, and Central West states. Tax reform should ensure revenue that instruments a regional development policy, so necessary for these regions. I believe this is a good opportunity for Parliament to reflect on a fundamental issue for the country, and that instead of dividing us, it should unite us. Fiscal warfare among states weakens federal relations and must be overcome. The Lula government reduced income inequality in Brazil, as never seen before, so we must think of a tax policy that perpetuates this achievement and does not deepen economic inequality among states. The President herself, Dilma, stated in her inauguration speech: "Only tax reform allows for sustainable expansion of industry and growth." We need to reflect on the tax reform we want. Or better yet, if we want a real reform or just a new regulation of ICMS. A reform demands an agenda of negotiations that does not only have a technical focus, but also considers regional realities and the notion of the country's development as a whole, where it does not make sense to label winners and losers. Similarly, Déda pondered on the issue of the pre-salt. Agreeing that producing states have a right to receive a larger share of royalties, the governor, however, defended a new distribution model, as this wealth belongs to the country and should serve it in its entirety. I have no doubt that the President has worked to ensure that the Northeast, North, and Central West have their benefits guaranteed and continue on the path of sustainable development and regional development to definitively overcome differences between South, Southeast, Northeast, North, and Central-West Brazil. Thank you.

epistemicQualifiers.claimText: that the link between the reform and the improvement of our representative democracy needs to be clearly emphasized
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: The aspirations of the entire Brazilian population, something that will hardly be achieved if we continue using the private financing system for election campaigns. I believe that the link between the reform and the improvement of our representative democracy needs to be clearly emphasized. Anyone who follows attentively the growing increase in the costs of election campaign activities knows that private influence has significantly increased in our electoral process. Candidates who are entirely dependent on private resources will not be able to fulfill their commitments to the entire population. Sooner or later, they will have to "account" to those who contributed decisively to their electoral success, either through support for projects that serve the specific interests of certain groups or even by sponsoring questionable proposals to various federal public administration bodies, in order to favor these same sponsors. At the same time, the establishment of exclusive public financing should be accompanied by a specific change in our proportional list representation system, which should transition from the current open list to a previously ordered list by political parties. While the list contributes to strengthening political life within our parties, with beneficial effects on their cohesion and programmatic construction, it also facilitates campaign expenditure oversight. Instead of personalized accounting, under the responsibility of each candidate taken individually, we will have a single account that centralizes the expenses of all candidates from the same party. At the same time, we believe that a closed list with public financing will reduce the costs of election campaigns, which are increasingly irrational due to the great uncertainty surrounding individual campaigns. On the other hand, our electoral process can also be improved through other specific initiatives in electoral rules. First, the end of the re-election of the President of the Republic, State Governors, and Mayors, an institution introduced in June 1997 and which, since then, has increased the power resources of elected officials, to the detriment of the principle of equality of conditions that should guide electoral disputes. At the same time, the long duration in office, allowed by the re-election institution, has contributed to the misuse of public machinery, especially in regions and states where civil society is less organized.

epistemicQualifiers.claimText: we should establish in our legisla- tion the obligation of "verticalization" of alliances, which should be organized in the states in a manner consistent with the agreements made in the construction of presidential slates
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: Similarly, we understand that the choice of all representatives of the people can be centralized in a single election, held every 5 years. Thus, instead of interrupting the legislative process and the greater difficulty for the proper functioning of the federal and state public administration due to the restrictions defined by electoral law, we would have the simultaneous renewal of all representatives of the people. At the same time, the elected officials would have 5 years to implement the proposals defended during the election campaigns, without losing continuity of work due to periodic elections every 2 years. Finally, I believe we should establish in our legisla- tion the obligation of "verticalization" of alliances, which should be organized in the states in a manner consistent with the agreements made in the construction of presidential slates. This measure has two main purposes: first, to contribute to the strengthening of the program- matic and ideological basis of political parties, avoid- ing opportunist alliances that, due to the peculiarities of our electoral system, allow state government candidates to ally with parties competing in different slates in the presidential elections; second, together with the end of alliances in proportional elections - a measure that will strengthen the larger parties - this would provide the elected President of the Republic greater ease in constru- ing his parliamentary base in the National Congress, even if his party, alone, has not achieved a majority of seats in Parliament. In summary, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, society is demanding from Parliament the changes necessary for our political system to be consistently prepared to accommodate the social, political, and economic advances the country has experienced in recent years. Thank you very much. MR. FERNANDO MARRONI (PT-RS. Without revision of the speaker) - Mr. President, I would like to highlight an important announcement by the Minister of Science and Technology, Aloizio Mercadante, regarding the con- struction of research ships so that Brazil can finally map its 4.5 million square kilometers of territorial sea. These ships will be built in Brazil and will be sponsored by PETROBRAS and Vale. With this, Brazil will also be able to conduct its own research and use these ships in Oceanography courses in our country. Thank you very much. STATEMENT DELIVERED BY THE SPEAKER

epistemicQualifiers.claimText: this news is of extreme importance for Brazil, as a country can only truly understand its full potential when it invests in research and innovation, especially in strategic areas such as territorial sea and exclusive economic zone
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, everyone who has been following us for decades, Brazil has dreamed of self-sufficiency in oil exploration, and it was only recently that it achieved this important milestone for the country's development through the discovery of oil in the pre-salt layer. This was made possible thanks to the valorization of PETROBRAS and the entire Brazilian research and innovation industry promoted by the Federal Government over the last decade. However, one last significant barrier remains: detailed knowledge of the entire Brazilian continental shelf. But this obstacle is expected to be overcome soon. Yesterday, Science and Technology Minister Aloizio Mercadante announced, during a meeting with representatives of the Navy in Rio de Janeiro, that Brazil will make the construction of research ships in new shipyards dedicated to mapping its territorial sea and exclusive economic zone a top naval priority. The Science and Technology Ministry wants to know in detail and as soon as possible the 4.5 million square kilometers of Brazilian territory located on the continental shelf, in order to identify economic potential, understand biodiversity, and study the effects of climate change and marine pollution on Brazil. This mapping is still in the planning phase, but the goal is for these ships, to be built with the highest technology in Brazilian shipyards, to also serve as a knowledge source for oceanography schools, ensuring an increasing number of specialized researchers. Look, gentlemen, at how important this can be for Brazil's future. As Minister Mercadante rightly said, it is one of the last strategic frontiers that the nation still needs to fully master technically. It is a challenge as great as the one we are overcoming today by expanding our knowledge of the Amazon rainforest to preserve the wealth it offers us, both economically and environmentally. These modern ships and the entire project to map the Brazilian continental shelf will be funded by ANP, interested in knowing the country's oil fields, and by PETROBRAS and Vale companies, which have economic interests in the continental shelf. I believe this news is of extreme importance for Brazil, as a country can only truly understand its full potential when it invests in research and innovation, especially in strategic areas such as territorial sea and exclusive economic zone.

Without revision of the speaker.) - Mr. President, ladies and gentlemen, I come to this podium to present a document that I delivered yesterday to Minister of Health, Alexandre Padilha, to propose the creation of the National Network for Attention and Support for Chemical Dependents and their Families. Crack is producing an epidemic in the public health of this country. It destroys lives, corrupts youth, and disrupts families. According to recent press reports - and today we have this issue as an editorial in Folha de S.Paulo - there are at least 1 million crack addicts in Brazil. Twenty years ago, crack use was limited to São Paulo. Today, the drug is present in 98% of Brazilian municipalities, due to the ease of obtaining it and its low price - a rock costs between 5 and 10 reais. Crack addicts young people from all socio-economic classes. According to experts, in many cases, it takes just one contact with the drug to create dependency. A recent study, conducted by Psychologist Maria de Fátima Padin, from the Federal University of São Paulo, which interviewed 500 family members of addicts and ex-addicts in São Paulo, mainly from classes A and B, reveals that, on average, parents took 2 and a half years to seek some type of help. Reasons for the delay: they didn't know what to do (30%); they thought they could solve the problem at home (24%); they thought drug use would be temporary (17%). Thirty-four percent initially turned to self-help groups and churches, and 11% asked for help from a psychiatrist. We cannot underestimate this violent and devastating enemy, but we should not be intimidated either. We need to provide answers. And I believe the answer is the creation of an integrated network for the treatment of dependents, where hospitalization and rehabilitation will be carried out.

epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: –, nonetheless, the number of registered participants has significantly increased and we want to give everyone the opportunity to speak before the end of the session. MR. EDSON SILVA (Block/PSB-CE. No speaker revision.) – Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, the most discussed topic in this House, both in the plenary and in the committees, is drugs and the involvement of young people with crack. All the newspaper articles we read express that Brazil is living an epidemic: young, violent protagonists, are killing and dying; and crack is the major force driving up violence in our country. On one hand, we see Federal, State, and Municipal Governments struggling to recover and save young people who are crack users. Federal resources for recovering alcohol dependents have fallen 45%, while resources for recovering drug and crack dependents have grown 70%. That means the Government is in a dilemma, not knowing who to attend to first. On the other hand – this is the reason that brings me to the podium –, we see the waste of money that could be applied to the recovery of drug dependents, particularly crack users. Every day, the Federal Revenue Service seizes contraband goods, goods that enter the country without paying taxes, which are then distributed and donated to various institutions, including many NGOs. I am unaware of the criteria for this donation. It is not known if, after the products are auctioned off, the money obtained is used for the benefit of the people and the country. Just now, the Federal Highway Police in Rio de Janeiro received truckloads of products seized by the Federal Revenue Service that mysteriously disappeared – the Federal Police is investigating this fact. In Ceará, the Federal Revenue Service donated truckloads of tires to the Fortaleza Air Base and other institutions. But the tires donated to the Fortaleza Air Base also mysteriously disappeared. What is the criterion adopted by the Federal Revenue Service for donating these seized products and monitoring whether the money raised from them is applied to a fair purpose? To conclude, Mr. President, I want to discuss here the creation of a national fund for the recovery of chemical dependents, in whose disposition the products seized by the Federal Revenue Service would fall. It is necessary to create a commission, a governing council, to auction off or sell these products, applying the obtained resources to this national fund. It seems to me that in this donation and distribution of products by the Federal Revenue Service, there is yet another diversion.

epistemicQualifiers.claimText: this should be a public policy: in addition to providing medicines for those with diabetes and hypertension, the government should also distribute continuous use medicines to those with other types of diseases
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: The purpose of a positive outcome, which meets the great needs of this country, especially the young people who are living on the streets, often resorting to drug use and dying. That was what I had to request, Mr. President. Mr. Reguffe (PDT-DF. No revision by the speaker.) - Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Parliamentarians, I return to this podium to defend a bill of my authorship that exempts medicines from taxes. In this country, 35.7% of the price of a medicine is made up of taxes. There are families that spend over 2,000 reais per month on continuous use medicines. It is absurd and unacceptable to charge the amount of taxes currently levied on a medicine. In countries like England, Canada, and Colombia, no taxes are paid on medicines. In the United States, 6.3% tax is levied on a medicine, and in Brazil, 35.7%. I made an information request to the Ministry of Finance, from which I received a response regarding the impact of this exemption on the Budget, which would be 3 billion reais per year. Well, the Union Budget is 2.73 trillion reais. The only thing that would happen is a reduction in the Union Budget from 2.73 trillion to 2.70 trillion - that is, a reduction of 3 billion reais. The impact would be minimal on the Union Budget (0.11%), and the state would make a direct contribution to improving the health of many people in this country. In my opinion, Mr. President, if a person has a disease, it is the state's responsibility to help them and facilitate access to the medicines they need. I have also made a recommendation to the Ministry of Finance to implement price controls and medicine pricing tables. The free market applies to various sectors of the economy, but not to those that affect people's lives, their health. No one can live or die and have their income as the defining factor. That is not fair! That is not right! I am also requesting a hearing with the Minister of Health, because I believe this should be a public policy: in addition to providing medicines for those with diabetes and hypertension, the government should also distribute continuous use medicines to those with other types of diseases. That is the state's role, its duty, that cannot act as if it were not its responsibility, as if this were not its problem. It is a problem, yes, of the state. I return to say: when a person has a disease, it is the state's responsibility to help them and facilitate their access to the medicines they need. Mr. President, I hope this House - and here I appeal to my colleagues - approves the project. It would be a significant step forward.

epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: Lastly, the secrecy of official documents cannot be left to the discretion of public officials. Nowhere does the law state that public officials are owners of these documents. These documents belong to the nation. The right to memory is common to all, without belonging to anyone in particular. Disclosing documents that, for state reasons, have become classified prevents the perpetuation of atrocities. They need to be disclosed at some point. They mitigate the face of authoritarian regimes. Omitting and concealing is the practice of spurious governments. We cannot acquiesce to this trend of the petist government to have a penchant for the pact of silence. I have been fighting this for over 60 days, since the decree of President Dilma was issued, in an attempt to reverse it, Deputy Praciano, because it is especially harmful to the North. The decree requires municipalities to bid, receive equipment, and start the work before the money is paid. I cite as an example programs like Calha Norte or programs of SUDAM, SUFRAMA, which do not have a convention with the Federal Savings Bank. It is a mistake by the Federal Government, and it is important that it be corrected. I am hoping that this decree will be extended. In fact, I have been obstructing for several weeks in this House so that this decree be extended and modified. I believe that the Federal Government can demand the completion of the bidding process up to the signing of the contract, but it cannot force, for example, the supplier to deliver a mechanized patrol without the guarantee that the municipality will pay, if the Federal Government has not yet transferred the resource. We cannot agree with this. Therefore, I request the extension and modification of the terms of the aforementioned decree, so that it covers the bidding and the contract, but not the delivery of equipment or the start of work. On the other hand, I want to provide information to the House and to Brazil, in my capacity as President of the Parliamentary Group Brazil-European Union.

epistemicQualifiers.claimText: that often the PT and PMDB come here to advocate for the end of coalitions
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: In the National Congress. If there had been no coalitions, or the possibility of coalitions, in 2010, the Workers' Party would have had 25 additional Deputies; the PMDB, 31; and six parties that are currently part of this House would have ceased to exist. That is why I believe that often the PT and PMDB come here to advocate for the end of coalitions. Well, they will grow; 26 and 31 Deputies would have been part of the base of these two parties if there had been no coalition. This is the logic of transferring, of concentrating in a few parties. This happens in an election; in the next one, the difference will be even greater. In a short time, we would have in Brazil two, three, or four parties, at most, because the small and medium-sized ones would be extinct. In addition to these parties, practically all the others would lose Deputies. My party, the PSB, for example, currently has 34 Deputies, and would have 29, losing 5; the DEM would lose 7 Deputies. I calculated, state by state, what the new reality would be if there had been no coalition. I am denouncing this because there is strong discussion in this House about the possibility of ending the coalition. If the end of the coalition comes with the end of the electoral coefficient, it will be possible to analyze. But I highly doubt that will happen. Therefore, I ask all parties that are not from the PMDB or PT to pay attention, because this will, in the short and medium term, be the end of the small and medium-sized parties in this House. I also want to register, Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Deputies, President Dilma's concern for the poorest. She is just, she is correct, she is consistent, but there is a great distortion between what she proposes and what the Federal Savings Bank, through a normative act, has been doing regarding the "My House, My Life" program. President Dilma proposes that the more poor people who have homes, the better. However, the normative act of the Federal Savings Bank states that in order to build homes under the "My House, My Life" program, there must be asphalt paving or any other type of paving. The problem is that many streets in several Brazilian municipalities are not paved, and the municipalities do not have the conditions to pave them. Therefore, exactly the most impoverished class of the cities is being excluded from this program, because the municipality cannot pave the streets, nor can the owner pave their own street. I also want to register that we are receiving today the distinguished visit of the Mayor of Cachoeirinha, Vicente Pires, who was called by President Dilma to participate in a meeting regarding the treatment of chemical dependents in the country.

"Many governments are coming to Pernambuco to see this management model that manages to save resources in maintenance and apply them to expanding public services," said Eduardo. Each secretary responsible for one of the six thematic rooms gave a brief overview, pointing out all the requests made during the meetings. In addition to them, Mr. President, three representatives from each room, chosen by the participants themselves, also had the microphone to share their observations. "Family farming and irrigation were the most discussed topics, along with the dairy chain in Afrânio," said Secretary Ranilson Ramos, who coordinated the Economic Development and Sustainability room. The São Francisco micro-region, in total, has seven municipalities: Afrânio, Cabrobó, Dormentes, Lagoa Grande, Orocó, Santa Maria da Boa Vista, and Petrolina, which hosted the event. All cities were represented at the seminar. In addition to listening to the population, the day was also marked by announcement of works. Taking advantage of the presence of National Integration Minister Fernando Bezerra Coelho, Eduardo signed four agreements. In total, the investments reach R$157 million, divided between the São Francisco and Parnaíba Valley Development Company (CODEVASF) and the State Government. The agreements were for water supply and sanitation works in Petrolina, totaling R$94.5 million. The tender for the construction of sanitation works in Ouricuri and Araripina was also launched, with values of R$32.5 million and R$29.8 million, respectively. The governor ended the first day of the marathon in the Sertão with a visit to the Gercino Coelho State School, which underwent a complete renovation worth R$1.7 million.

epistemicQualifiers.claimText: that we have to start exactly from this point
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: distant locations from cities, from highways. This distance alone makes settlements unviable. Evidence of this is that, after 10, 20 years, some settled families end up selling their property and buying a small farm, a property on the outskirts of a city, in order for their lives to improve. It seems to me that we have to start exactly from this point. Land reform can be more expensive at first, because the Government will have to buy land along the highways, but in the medium and long term, it will be cheaper and more viable, as we won't have family evictions, as in current settlements. The INCRA settled families 10, 12 years ago, and the infrastructure has still not been resolved. Governments have been working under pressure. Some families moved to those Northern states, mainly Pará; a large part went to Maranhão and Piauí; and many others sought better days in government-incented programs, in mines. Now, these families have no way back, have no other employment alternative and need to seek survival on the land. It's time to rethink land reform. For 30 years, since I arrived in the state of Pará, I have been a defender of land reform in the Amazon. The development of family farming in the Amazon will only be possible if settlements are made along the rivers or along the highways. The state of Pará today has over 5,000 kilometers of federal highways, many already paved, others in the process of paving, such as Cuiabá-Santarém and Transamazônica. Probably, by the end of 2014, they will all be 100% paved. Just these two highways have a distance of 2,000 kilometers, and many lands along these highways could be bought by the Federal Government and designated for family settlement. Thus, of course, energy will come more easily, the doctor will come more easily, educational follow-up, school transport, production will come more easily to the cities - freight is lower, and what families need to buy also arrives at a lower price. Today, the opposite occurs: what is produced is sold at a lower price and other products are bought at a higher price. In this exchange, there is impoverishment, dis-capitalization and bankruptcy of many families settled by INCRA. Another point: infrastructure. It's no use implementing the "Light for All" program, a policy that deserves commendations. We need to advance in providing electric power to all communities. In the state of Pará, there are communities that have electric power, and farmers even set up a small factory there to produce cheese during the period...

DEPUTE IZALCI (Parliamentary Bloc/PR - DF - Unrevised by the speaker): Mr. President, ladies and gentlemen, today's Correio Braziliense carries an article titled And the lobby won. This article, Mr. President, deals with a bill, whose authorship I'm not sure of. When I was in the Legislative Assembly, I presented a bill like this one, which was put on the voting agenda, but it was withdrawn, and the bill was not voted on. It seems that later, another deputy pre- sented the same bill, and yesterday, at a meeting of the Constitutional and Legal Affairs Commission in the Legislative Assembly, it was archived. The bill, Mr. President, deals with the hiring of compa- nies by Parliamentarians in the Federal District Govern- ment. I presented a bill in the Legislative Assembly pro- hibiting the executive, legislative, and accounting au- thorities from hiring companies whose partners are de- puties or relatives up to the third degree. Unfortunately, I was unable to get it passed in that house. In the previous term, here in the Chamber of Depu- ties, I had the opportunity to present the same bill. Since I was serving in the Secretariat, I did not follow its pro- gression very closely. It went through this House, and here it may have lost its essence, because the bill deals with prohibiting the hiring and even the conclusion of agreements with institutions and companies. In this House, they removed the terms "contract" and "hiring," leaving only "agreements." I am now working to change that, to retrieve the term "contracts" in the Senate, be- cause I believe this is a relevant issue, and this House needs to take these measures so that the executive, par- ticularly, does not hire companies linked to authorities. The most serious thing that has been happening, Mr. President, is that most of the contracts are being made in the form of emergency contracts, that is, they do not even participate in bidding processes. Today's article says that for these companies linked to deputies, 773 mil- lion reais were paid. Just this year, 2011, almost 80 mil- lion reais were paid to companies linked to deputies. And many of these contracts are emergency contracts.

epistemicQualifiers.claimText: that the total or partial transformation of the conservation unit into units of the Integral Protection Group or the Sustainable Use Group, provided that the procedures outlined in Article 22, clause 2 of the SNUC Law are followed, should be carried out through a normative instrument of the same hierarchical level that created it
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: Brazilian, and that this advertising should be given in the best way to reach its target audience. I share the understanding of the distinguished author that the creation of a Private Natural Heritage Reserve (PNHR) arises from the noble intention of the private land owner. It is important to note that the mere intention of the owner does not suffice to create a PNHR; it is necessary for there to be, on site, a diversity of biology (defined in Article 2, clause III of the Law of the National System of Conservation Units - SNUC) that justifies the creation of the conservation unit. And, as a conservation unit, the PNHR is not only permanently registered but is also strictly subject to a series of procedural and regulatory implications, including normative ones, aimed at preserving and conserving the ecosystems, species, and natural habitats present in the PNHR. The constitutional principles guide the "mens legis," constituting a limitation on the legislator's actions. In this context, the principle of equality, enshrined in our Magna Carta, stands out; it is not enough for the legislator to ensure that the law is clear and objective; he must also ensure that its application by the interpreter is done with equality. Therefore, it is the legislator's responsibility not only to provide equal normative treatment to situations of equality but also to provide unequal normative treatment to situations of inequality; primarily, he must ensure that this treatment is justified, reasonable, proportional, feasible, and effective. Under this perspective, as a parliamentarian and as a citizen, I am fully aware of how the exercise of the legislative power reflects and impacts, directly and indirectly, the life of Brazilian society, of which we are legitimate representatives. Thus, imbued with a spirit of collaboration and guided by the principles that govern parliamentary action, as enshrined in the Magna Carta, I consider it necessary to adjust the Law of SNUC, regarding conservation units, in order to harmonize and standardize equivalent situations, currently treated normatively in a context of inequality that is not justifiable. I believe that the total or partial transformation of the conservation unit into units of the Integral Protection Group or the Sustainable Use Group, provided that the procedures outlined in Article 22, clause 2 of the SNUC Law are followed, should be carried out through a normative instrument of the same hierarchical level that created it. Well, in August 1997, Cel Uyrangê Bolívar Soares Nogueira de Houanda, retired from the Air Force, granted an interview to ufologists Ademar Gevaerd and Marco Petit, also recorded on video, which I possess, where he relates information, I believe, relevant to the subject of UFOs - Unidentified Flying Objects. Obviously, going into details would be tedious, especially because they are mentioned in my first letter. Therefore, my question is simple

epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: Therefore, I have decided to write to you requesting access to the films and photographs, as I believe this material is in the possession of COMDABRA (as I understand, the former NUCOMDABRA), which, according to a letter addressed to the late Dr. Osny Schwan, was the organization responsible for cataloging and analyzing OVNI (unidentified flying objects) at the time, commanded by Air Brigadier Ronald Eduardo Jaeckel. I reiterate that the statements made here were by Cell Uyrangê and Commander Gerson de Brito. Unfortunately, Mr. Uyrangê passed away in October, but his statements were recorded on video. I kindly request that if this material is not in the possession of COMDABRA, at least inform me of the organization that currently holds it. I reaffirm, with conviction, the prerogatives of the initial letter, that is, the subject is controversial without a doubt, but real. Unfortunately, due to the stigma of esotericism and other adjectives, the difficulty of believing in the phenomenon is so great that the very unusualness of it takes care of the cover-up.

epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: I witnessed a strange phenomenon in the sky last night. Around 10 PM, I saw a bright, circular object moving at an incredible speed. It was unlike anything I've ever seen before, and it quickly disappeared from view. I'm not sure what it was, but it left me with a sense of wonder and mystery. II - Several people in my neighborhood reported similar sightings last night. They described seeing a UFO (unidentified flying object) with lights that seemed to change colors as it moved. Some even claimed to have seen it for several minutes before it vanished. III - The local police received multiple calls about the incident, but they were unable to locate the object or identify any potential witnesses. They suggested that it might have been a weather phenomenon or a military aircraft, but the descriptions from witnesses don't match any known aircraft models. IV - Today, I've been trying to reach out to experts in the field of ufology to discuss this event. I want to understand if there's any scientific explanation for what I saw or if it's something more extraordinary. I'm hoping to gain some clarity and perhaps contribute to the ongoing study of these mysterious sky objects.

epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: I witnessed a strange phenomenon in the sky last night. At around 10 PM, I saw a bright, circular object moving at an incredible speed. It was unlike anything I've ever seen before, and it quickly disappeared from view. I'm not sure what it was, but it left me feeling both intrigued and slightly unnerved. I've heard reports of similar sightings in the area, with some people claiming it was a UFO. However, I can't confirm if that's what I saw. It could have been a rare atmospheric phenomenon or perhaps a secret military aircraft. The speed and agility of the object were truly remarkable. I plan to keep an eye out for any further unusual activity and will report any new observations. This experience has definitely sparked my curiosity about the unknown.

epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: - ------ 3/13/69 - 7:40 PM - Jane Garavello, a witness, reported seeing a strange object in the sky. In addition to other lights, she observed a cylindrical object with two lights at its ends. She stated that it flew over a football field at a low altitude. We later verified this with the owner of the property, whose son had also seen the object. No other observations were made at that time; the object could not be located on the grass due to the darkness. I intend to return to the scene and gather more evidence. As you can see, Major, these are the details of the incident. I believe that with further investigation, we can determine what this object was.

epistemicQualifiers.claimText: what it was
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: I witnessed a strange phenomenon in the sky last night. Around 10 PM, I saw a bright, circular object moving at an incredible speed. It was unlike anything I've ever seen before, and it quickly disappeared from view. I'm not sure what it was, but it left me with a sense of wonder and mystery. II - Several people in my neighborhood reported similar sightings last night. They described seeing a UFO (unidentified flying object) with lights that seemed to change colors as it moved. Some even claimed to have seen it for several minutes before it vanished. III - The local police received multiple calls about the incident, but they were unable to locate the object or identify any potential witnesses. They suggested that it might have been a weather phenomenon or a military aircraft, but the descriptions from witnesses don't match any known aircraft models. IV - Today, I've been trying to reach out to experts in the field of ufology to discuss this event. I want to understand if there's any scientific explanation for what I saw or if it's something more extraordinary. I'm hoping to gain some clarity and perhaps contribute to the ongoing study of these mysterious sky objects.

epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: I witnessed a strange phenomenon in the sky last night. Around 10 PM, I saw a bright, circular object moving at an incredible speed. It was unlike anything I've ever seen before, and it quickly disappeared from view. I'm not sure what it was, but it left me with a sense of wonder and mystery. II - Several people in my neighborhood reported similar sightings last night. They described seeing a UFO (unidentified flying object) with lights that seemed to change colors as it moved. Some even claimed to have seen it for several minutes before it vanished. III - The local police received multiple calls about the incident, but they were unable to locate the object or identify any potential witnesses. They suggested that it might have been a weather phenomenon or a military aircraft, but the descriptions from witnesses don't match any known aircraft models. IV - Today, I've been trying to reach out to experts in the field of ufology to discuss this event. I want to understand if there's any scientific explanation for what I saw or if it's something more extraordinary. I'm hoping to gain some clarity and perhaps contribute to the ongoing study of these mysterious sky objects.

epistemicQualifiers.claimText: saw it first
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: FLYING SAUCER? “I don't want to be photographed! This flying saucer is making my life hell.” That was how Sergio Apolonio greeted the reporters who were seeking details about a flying saucer that reportedly flew over Santo André last Friday. He was nervous and seemed not to have slept well. “I can't take another step in this city without someone asking me about that flying saucer. I don't even know whether it was a saucer; it was a light that moved.” The patrons of the bar O Canario de Prata were the ones who saw the strange object. It was approximately 19 hours last Friday, and they were having their usual aperitif: “Look, there's a strange object.” “Where?” “There, between the Sears building and the Brasil building.” Soon all the bar's patrons went out onto Campos Salles street and tried to follow every movement of the unexpected object. Justice of the Peace Francisco Cardoso Franco, who lives on the corner, heard the men's commotion and came out into the street: “If what I saw is a flying saucer, I saw a flying saucer.” The judge says he saw a light moving horizontally from west to east, but does not think it was a saucer. Another witness to the strange light over Santo André is Marcio Mondes, who works at the Souza Cruz cigarette company: “It was a light that flashed intermittently. It was not a satellite, because I have had the opportunity to observe satellites passing. It was something very strange. The light was like that of a star, but we could not make out a central nucleus or anything similar.” Sergio Apolonio did not want photographs and explained: “Of the group that saw the saucer, I am the best known in the city. They call my home without stopping. I work in advertising and draw fashion designs, and I think something like this could harm my career. I want to be known for my art, not as the man who saw the flying saucer. My colleagues have already started joking, and this could go a long way if I do not put a stop to it.” Apolonio draws the mysterious object's route and comments: “It was first seen here above the Sears building, then slowly moved horizontally until it passed the Brasil building. We went to the corner and watched the object's movement, using the electricity and telephone wires as reference points. At one point the object began moving vertically. It rose in a kind of zigzag and then grew smaller until it disappeared completely.” Mixirica, a young man who serves at the counter of O Canario de Prata, gives his account: “It was approximately seven o'clock. The usual crowd was at the counter having an aperitif and chatting. I do not know who saw it first, but soon we all went out to see that light. There were about ten or fifteen people there.” Many people saw this mysterious object that flew over Santo André last Friday, but the skeptics are not convinced. A salesman with a brown briefcase says ironically: “These people are seeing things. To me, that was the Pirelli helicopter.”

epistemicQualifiers.claimText: in the existence of life on other plan- ets because the evidence is there
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: that we would be watched. If we, within all these scientifically proven principles, are constantly spying on the Universe, wouldn't someone else be doing the same? And since they are more advanced, they would obviously have better conditions to study us. | It is not the fact that science proves certain principles that would lead us not to accept contrary things. It just so happens that these same principles could be "used by other beings in a different way. Once proven scientifically here, it is clear that it applies to the entire Universe. From the moment a study is taken to a higher level, one could never reach a conclusion with just two answers. And NASA did just that in one of its expeditions. If it was not proven to exist, how can they say it is true? Also, no one has been able to make someone retract such a statement. They saw it, period, and that's it! Is it possible that in a Universe so infinitely vast, there is only us? Currently, at the same time a program is airing in Sweden, we can watch it at home, tranquilly; in the future, a camera will be on Saturn, and you will also be able to see it in the same way. Perhaps no cameras will even be needed. From here, we would tune in to what we are supposed to see. Wouldn't that happen in their civil- ization right now? Despite all of this, I believe in the existence of life on other plan- ets because the evidence is there. But to recognize this truth, we can never look at them through the limited human perspective. The world is vast, and the knowledge that emerges is also vast, and what does man know about himself? What about the others? Benny Shamss - Capital.

epistemicQualifiers.claimText: that every person who proposes to opine on a subject, directly or indirectly, is concerned with it
epistemicQualifiers.evidenceExcerpt: | To: Mr. Editor; I request, at your kindness, to include this letter in your section, necessary for the proper understanding of a matter of great importance. | Regarding: A response to your letter, "LAST MINUTE, 24/4/1969," concerning the problematic and disturbing issue of flying saucers. | It is undeniable that flying saucers are a subject that arouses curiosity, ignites discussions, and in the minds of enlightened individuals, lights the flame of an ideal, that is, contact with them. However, in view of this, while many people have undertaken positive research, information, and clarification efforts regarding flying saucers, it is also necessary to state that just as many individuals have used the same issue for questionable purposes, without integrity or moderation. This group includes Mr. José A. da Silva. This gentleman, to my knowledge, has but one purpose: to "appear." | Mr. José A. da Silva: I am opposed to the polemic, having taken into consideration your aforementioned letter, in response to Mr. Reginaldo in this same forum, and totally disagreeing with it, I reserve the right to express my contrary opinion. | Dear Sir, I believe that every person who proposes to opine on a subject, directly or indirectly, is concerned with it. You, therefore, are not the exception to the rule. Given this, flying saucers concern us, despite your formal denial of their existence. | My dear Sir, if my assertion is correct, I believe you should respect my opinion, even if it is levian. | If, on the other hand, I am in error, you are wasting your time, not to mention annoying readers with your chatter. Let us then come to what you have to say. In your letter, you cited a well-known scientist, Dr. Herman W. Oberth, and used a mystical term, besides distorting the truth to make us believe that the cited scientist, propagating what would be a condemnable lie. | My dear Sir, your opinion is unconvincing, levian, and imbued with bad faith. You cast a disreputable statement over the name of a scientific person, one that you cannot prove, nor do you present arguments to support it. | Since this is the case, it has sufficed for me to make a superficial reading of your letter to understand that you do not have the slightest regard for men of science. This does not surprise me, as it seems to me that you are the type who believes he knows it all, and that the world and its events always revolve around him.
